title: Prose workflow was not followed
statement: A real tanstack-dashboard implementation session had the sunset-pathfinder code available but made zero state-init, cartographer_state, compact-generate, or state-resume calls.

title: Missing state was not a gitignore effect
statement: The inspected worktree ignored only .cartographer/current.json; the absence of .cartographer/<topic>/state.json was because the workflow never initialized state.

title: Pi compaction differs from Cartographer state compaction
statement: The session had Pi transcript compaction events, but those did not write Cartographer .cartographer state because compact-generate was never called.

title: Final response can drift from plan state
statement: The analyzed session ended with later tanstack-dashboard phases still pending while the final assistant response described the cleanup as done.

title: ADR-0004 chose state-backed single writer
statement: ADR-0004 establishes parent/current-agent single-writer implementation with .cartographer state, compact-generate, state-resume, deterministic receipts, and read-only gates.

title: Current implement skill remains prose-driven
statement: skills/implement/SKILL.md documents state and compact commands, but the skill itself cannot force the model to call them.

title: State CLI already implements primitives
statement: cartographer_state.ts already exposes state-init, state-validate, state-set-next, state-set-working-set, state-record-validation-ref, journal-append, current-set, compact-generate, and state-resume.

title: Existing state tests use temp roots
statement: tests/cartographer_state.test.ts proves state files are created under temp projects, semantic commands mutate state, and state-resume is read-only.

title: Pi extensions can enforce workflow preflight
statement: Pi extensions can register commands/tools and intercept lifecycle events including input, before_agent_start, context, tool_call, and session compaction hooks.

title: Pi tool_call hooks can block unsafe actions
statement: Pi tool_call event handlers can block a tool call by returning a block result and can mutate tool input before execution.

title: Pi compaction hooks can bridge state compaction
statement: Pi exposes session_before_compact and session_compact hooks, allowing Cartographer to run or record state compaction around transcript compaction.

title: Pi SDK enables deeper runtime orchestration
statement: The Pi SDK exposes AgentSession, AgentSessionRuntime, prompt/follow-up APIs, event subscriptions, compaction, and runtime replacement hooks for future command-runner integration.

title: Planning graph validator can guard finalization
statement: validate_planning_graph.py already detects completed phase evidence gaps and can be extended or wrapped to block final success when executable phases remain pending.

title: Auditor gate principles remain required
statement: ADR-0002 requires deterministic validation evidence and read-only semantic review principles that the wrapper should preserve rather than bypass.

title: Wrapper overreach risk
statement: A wrapper that edits too much hidden state or auto-drives commits could become another opaque orchestrator; it should keep .plan authoritative and expose compact receipts/state transitions.

title: Use temp roots in tests
statement: Tests for wrapper state, .plan, .cartographer, index, and receipt behavior must use temp/mock roots rather than the repository's real planning artifacts.

title: Skill-prose enforcement gap
statement: If implementation remains prose-only, future agents can ignore state initialization, misinterpret transcript compaction as workflow compaction, and stop after partial phases.

title: Subagent handoff output capture needs deterministic wrapper
statement: The proposal should include a deterministic subagent handoff wrapper because recent auditor retries showed that read-only semantic gates can suffer harness/report-capture friction distinct from semantic PASS/FAIL outcomes.

title: Subagents dependency should be evaluated before replacement
statement: The observed subagent friction is evidence to quarantine generic subagent calls behind a Cartographer-specific handoff API and evaluate reliability metrics before deciding to patch or replace the dependency with a Cartographer-native Pi SDK runner.

title: Skills should not own deterministic mutations
statement: Cartographer skills should describe workflow intent and UX, while deterministic tools/scripts should own high-impact artifact mutation, state transitions, validation gates, and finalization checks.

title: Proposal initialization should be deterministic
statement: Proposal directory/file initialization is currently described in prose and should be handled by a proposal init wrapper to avoid missing skeleton artifacts or accidental truncation.

title: Fact graph appends need a wrapper
statement: Source-backed fact and supported_by edge creation is currently model-mediated and should be wrapped so cited facts are always supported and valid JSONL.

title: Plan status updates need atomic synchronization
statement: Manual updates to plan.md checkboxes/statuses and plan.nodes.jsonl can desynchronize; a plan status wrapper should update both atomically.

title: Context packs need deterministic creation
statement: Context packs are gate inputs that agents can forget; a context-pack wrapper should create/update bounded records from verified artifacts and receipt IDs.

title: Proposal and plan finalization need wrappers
statement: Proposal and plan acceptance currently combine validation, citation checks, context packs, subagent audit, and receipts through prose; finalize wrappers should enforce those gates deterministically.

title: Plan graph generation should be deterministic
statement: Plan graph JSONL should be generated or reconciled from plan.md by a script rather than hand-authored in parallel by the agent.

title: Generic non-validation receipts need schema enforcement
statement: Validation receipts have a runner, but fallback, audit, timeout, compass, phase, output-capture, and legacy-bypass receipts are often appended manually and need a schema-checked receipt wrapper.

title: Validation item completion should verify receipts
statement: A validation item should not be marked complete unless a deterministic wrapper verifies that a matching passed receipt exists.

title: ADR metadata synchronization should be deterministic
statement: Proposal and plan ADR metadata should be synchronized with cartographer_adr evaluation output or require an explicit override rationale, instead of relying on manual prose updates.

title: Proposal skill
description: Current proposal workflow prose for skeleton creation, fact graph appends, ADR metadata, validation, and audit gates.

title: Plan skill
description: Current planning workflow prose for plan graph creation, phase status, validation, compass/auditor gates, and finalization.

title: Lifecycle transitions need a deterministic gate
statement: Cartographer should have a cartographer_transition wrapper that verifies prerequisites, records transition receipts, and blocks proposal, plan, phase, and implementation lifecycle changes until gates are satisfied.

title: Human approvals should be explicit transition receipts
statement: Human-in-the-loop approval should stop the workflow at proposal, plan, phase, and final implementation review gates, then resume only after cartographer_transition approve records an auditable approval receipt.

title: Approver identity should default deterministically
statement: cartographer_transition approve should allow explicit --approved-by, otherwise resolve approver identity from gitignored .cartographer/config.toml, then git config user.name, then the system username.

title: Open workflow questions resolved by user
statement: The user selected hyphenated CLI aliases, explicit CI approver identity, hybrid edit guardrails, and evidence-based subagent dependency evaluation with other extensions considered before building a native runner.

title: Open questions decision receipt
description: Plan-phase decision receipt recording the user's selected options for open workflow questions.

title: Implementation phases advance automatically by default
statement: Human approval is required for proposal-to-plan, plan-to-implementation, and final implementation approval; individual implementation phases should advance automatically after deterministic prerequisites unless a plan explicitly marks a phase as human-gated.
